beats.label: S1 · Two centuries later
beats.text: Ichabod beheads the Headless Horseman in a 1781 battle and wakes in 2013 Sleepy Hollow, occultly bound to the creature by shared blood.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the premise and the blood link that constrains every later attempt to kill the Horseman.

beats.label: S1 · The Witnesses
beats.text: Lt Abbie Mills, whose mentor Corbin was killed by the Horseman, becomes Ichabod's partner; his archives reveal the two of them are the biblical Witnesses.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the central duo and the archive that funds every case in the show; the Witness identity anchors everything after.

beats.label: S1 · Moloch's Apocalypse
beats.text: The Horseman is Death, sent by the demon Moloch to summon the other three and start the Apocalypse; Katrina, executed for witchcraft, guides Ichabod from purgatory.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's villain and stakes, and introduces Katrina as the wife trapped on the other side.

beats.label: S1 · Abraham unmasked
beats.text: Interrogating the captured Horseman, Ichabod learns it is Abraham Van Brunt — his old friend, Katrina's former fiancé — turned undead by Moloch after Hessians killed him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Horseman becomes personal; sets up the love triangle that steers Katrina's choices for two more seasons.

beats.label: S1 · A son in purgatory
beats.text: Ichabod ventures into purgatory to speak with Katrina and discovers they had a son, Jeremy, born while she took magical sanctuary from the coven that condemned her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The son revelation is the seed that pays off catastrophically in the finale; no Jeremy, no Henry twist.

beats.label: S1 · Enter Henry Parrish
beats.text: Sin eater Henry Parrish severs Ichabod's blood tie to the Horseman and joins the Witnesses' inner circle, helping them plan the final defense against Moloch.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the trusted mentor who will invert into the season's central betrayal; a viewer must remember he was welcomed inside.

beats.label: S1 · The betrayal
beats.text: Henry reveals he is Jeremy — the Horseman of War — buries Ichabod alive, hands Katrina to the Horseman, traps Abbie in purgatory, and breaks the second seal of the Apocalypse.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The cliffhanger itself; every S2 plot line begins from one of these four positions.

cliffhanger.text: Henry, Ichabod and Katrina's son, has revealed himself as the Horseman of War, freed the Headless Horseman, handed Katrina to him, buried Ichabod alive, and trapped Abbie in purgatory. Moloch's second seal is broken and the Apocalypse has begun.
questions: Can Ichabod escape his coffin before he suffocates?
With Abbie trapped in purgatory and Katrina in the Horseman's grasp, who is left to stand against Moloch?
Is there any part of Jeremy still reachable, or is War now Moloch's forever?

characters.name: Ichabod Crane
characters.line: 1781 soldier revived in 2013 as one of the two biblical Witnesses; buried alive by his own son at season's end.

characters.name: Abbie Mills
characters.line: The other Witness, a Sleepy Hollow lieutenant who inherited Corbin's occult files; now trapped in purgatory in Katrina's place.

characters.name: Katrina Crane
characters.line: Ichabod's witch wife, freed briefly from purgatory before being handed to the Horseman by their son as his reward.

characters.name: Henry Parrish / Jeremy Crane
characters.line: Introduced as a trustworthy sin eater; revealed as Ichabod and Katrina's son, resurrected by Moloch as the Horseman of War.

characters.name: The Headless Horseman / Abraham Van Brunt
characters.line: Death of the Four Horsemen; Ichabod's old friend and Katrina's former fiancé, killed by Hessians and turned by Moloch.

characters.name: Jenny Mills
characters.line: Abbie's estranged sister and former asylum patient; Corbin's other apprentice, well versed in the occult and heavily armed.

characters.name: Frank Irving
characters.line: Sleepy Hollow police captain, jailed after confessing to murders his possessed daughter committed in order to shield her.

characters.name: Moloch
characters.line: The demon commanding the Horsemen from purgatory; architect of the Apocalypse now unfolding in Sleepy Hollow.

beats.label: S2 · Rescue from purgatory
beats.text: Ichabod uses a key hidden by Franklin to pull Abbie back from purgatory; Katrina stays behind, planning to spy on Henry and the Horseman from inside their camp.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets the Witness pairing and puts Katrina inside the enemy household, which drives the whole season's information flow.

beats.label: S2 · Irving signed away
beats.text: Henry poses as Irving's lawyer and tricks him into signing their contract in blood, quietly making Irving's soul Henry's property.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up why Irving is the only one who can wield the soul-eating sword later.

beats.label: S2 · Moloch inside Katrina
beats.text: Katrina's illness turns out to be a pregnancy — the fetus is Moloch, being reborn through her — and Ichabod and Abbie exorcise the demon before it can gestate.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Moloch has to accelerate his plan and why Katrina's link to him lingers after.

beats.label: S2 · The Sword of Methuselah
beats.text: The Witnesses find a sword that kills any supernatural being but takes the wielder's soul; only Irving, already soulless from the contract, can safely bear it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The weapon whose price sets up Irving's death in the finale.

beats.label: S2 · Moloch destroyed
beats.text: Irving sacrifices himself striking down the Horseman of War; ordered to murder Katrina, Henry instead turns the sword on Moloch and destroys him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the series' first big bad and puts Henry and Katrina at a loss — the state that produces Katrina's descent.

beats.label: S2 · Katrina turns dark
beats.text: Two months on, Katrina embraces dark magic and shields Abraham from destruction, straining her marriage with Ichabod; a memory-less Irving mysteriously returns from the dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The pivot from ally to antagonist; without this, her final act is inexplicable.

beats.label: S2 · Katrina killed in 1781
beats.text: After Ichabod kills Henry, Katrina flees to 1781 to erase him from history; he stabs her to save Abbie, returning to the present a widower alongside a freed Irving.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the emotional starting position for S3: Ichabod alone with Abbie, having killed the wife he crossed two centuries for.

cliffhanger.text: Moloch, Henry and Katrina are all dead — Katrina by Ichabod's own hand in 1781, after she tried to erase him from history. Irving is back and freed of his contract, but Ichabod is a widower and the Headless Horseman still walks free.
questions: What is left of the Witness partnership after Ichabod chose Abbie over his wife?
Can Ichabod live with having killed the woman he crossed two centuries to save?
With Moloch gone, what evil moves into the vacuum in Sleepy Hollow?

characters.name: Ichabod Crane
characters.line: Witness and now widower after stabbing Katrina in 1781 to save Abbie.

characters.name: Abbie Mills
characters.line: Witness, rescued from purgatory and now the person Ichabod chose over his wife.

characters.name: Jenny Mills
characters.line: Full member of the team; helped her sister uncover their mother's death and finally lay it to rest.

characters.name: Frank Irving
characters.line: Police captain freed from Henry's blood contract; mysteriously returned from the dead, memory now restored.

characters.name: Katrina Crane
characters.line: Dead. Killed by Ichabod in 1781 after turning to dark magic and travelling back to erase him from time.

characters.name: Henry Parrish / Jeremy Crane
characters.line: Dead. Killed by Ichabod while trying to reawaken Sleepy Hollow's ancient witches.

characters.name: The Headless Horseman / Abraham
characters.line: Still at large; Katrina persuaded him to give up his vendetta against Ichabod before her death.

beats.label: S3 · Nine months later
beats.text: Abbie is now an FBI agent when Ichabod resurfaces with Katrina's darkened pendant — the Horseman has vanished, and a new threat has taken his place in Sleepy Hollow.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets the status quo and signals the villain handoff from Moloch's world to something older.

beats.label: S3 · Pandora and her tree
beats.text: A woman named Pandora seals the Horseman in a box and looses fear-eating demons; each victim's terror fertilises a strange tree in her lair, one blossom at a time.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's antagonist and the ticking-clock mechanism she is using.

beats.label: S3 · The Hidden One
beats.text: Pandora is a Sumerian sorceress reviving her husband, the Hidden One — a fallen deity once made to guard the box of the world's evils, now bent on remaking humanity.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals the season's real villain and reframes Pandora as a servant, not the head of the plot.

beats.label: S3 · Abbie disappears
beats.text: To stop the Hidden One weaponising a magical Shard, Abbie carries its unstable energy through Pandora's tree into another dimension and vanishes for what proves to be ten months.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The mid-season absence that changes Abbie and plants the corruption she brings back.

beats.label: S3 · Marked on return
beats.text: Ichabod astral-projects into that ruined world; Abbie escapes through a well but returns branded with a symbol she has secretly pledged herself to — the Emblem of Thura.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains Abbie's later hesitation and the pull she cannot name; the symbol is the second half of the season's mythology.

beats.label: S3 · Uneasy alliance
beats.text: Stripped of her power by the Hidden One, Pandora offers to help the Witnesses reforge her box and trap him inside; Betsy Ross's hidden clues lead them to the temple's catacombs.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The tactical premise of the finale — a viewer needs to understand why Pandora is at their side by the last episode.

beats.label: S3 · Abbie's sacrifice
beats.text: Sealing the Hidden One inside the box requires a Witness's soul. Abbie sacrifices herself; Ichabod is told her soul will reawaken in another Witness he must now find.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The single beat S4 exists to answer; without this, S4's DC setup makes no sense.

cliffhanger.text: Abbie is dead. Ichabod, told her soul will be reborn in another Witness, is leaving Sleepy Hollow for Washington with a secret order founded by Washington himself. Jenny's long-absent father has just reappeared with information about the order.
questions: Whose body now carries Abbie's soul?
What does Washington's secret order want from Ichabod?
What does Jenny's father know that he came back to tell her?

characters.name: Ichabod Crane
characters.line: Grieving Witness leaving Sleepy Hollow for Washington to find the person carrying Abbie's reborn soul.

characters.name: Abbie Mills
characters.line: Dead. Gave her own soul to seal the Hidden One inside Pandora's box.

characters.name: Jenny Mills
characters.line: Sole surviving Mills sister; killed the mortal Hidden One and reconnected with her long-absent father.

characters.name: Joe Corbin
characters.line: Sheriff Corbin's son and Jenny's love interest; killed in his wendigo form during the final battle.

characters.name: Pandora
characters.line: Sumerian sorceress and wife of the Hidden One; killed by the resurrected Horseman in Ichabod's final act of revenge.

characters.name: The Hidden One
characters.line: Sumerian deity revived by Pandora; stripped of his powers into the box and killed, mortal, by Jenny.

beats.label: S4 · Agency 355
beats.text: Weeks after Abbie's death, Ichabod partners with DHS agent Diana Thomas and joins Agency 355 in Washington to hunt the demon Booth once used to kill Lincoln.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the new setting, the new team, and Diana as the person the whole season's arc rests on.

beats.label: S4 · The next Witness
beats.text: A prophetic dream leads Ichabod to Diana's young daughter Molly: she is the reincarnation of Abbie's soul, the second Witness he was sent to find.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the S3 cliffhanger and rearranges the Witness pairing around a child and her mother.

beats.label: S4 · Malcolm Dreyfuss
beats.text: Tech mogul Malcolm Dreyfuss, who once sold his soul to the demon Jobe for the life he was meant to have, hunts the fragments of the Philosopher's Stone to seize immortality.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's villain and the artefact-quest that structures every case up to the finale.

beats.label: S4 · Immortality traded
beats.text: Ichabod learns Washington had made him immortal via the Stone; Dreyfuss destroys the Stone but drinks an elixir of the Horseman's blood, taking that immortality for himself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Ichabod's plot armour and gives the villain his; sets the terms of the finale.

beats.label: S4 · Lara from the future
beats.text: A time-traveller named Lara — Molly, grown up — arrives to stop Dreyfuss's tyranny; warned that Diana is fated to become the Horseman of War, Ichabod takes the mantle himself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's turning point; changes who Ichabod is and what the team is fighting to prevent.

beats.label: S4 · Deal with the Devil
beats.text: Lara talks Ichabod back from War; a resurrected, gentler Henry takes the mantle instead. Ichabod bargains his soul to Lucifer for a new Stone to undo Dreyfuss's immortality.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the price of victory that the finale — and Ichabod's future — will be paid in.

beats.label: S4 · Freedom, on credit
beats.text: Diana shoots the newly mortal Dreyfuss and Jobe drags his forfeit soul to Hell; Agency 355 is reinstated and Ichabod granted citizenship — but his soul now belongs to Lucifer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The final state of every character and the unresolved debt hanging over Ichabod.

cliffhanger.text: Dreyfuss is dead, Agency 355 is reinstated, and Ichabod is finally an American citizen with a new partner and a new Witness. But he has sold his soul to Lucifer for the Philosopher's Stone, and the debt has not yet come due.
questions: How does Ichabod intend to buy his soul back from Lucifer?
What does it mean for the Witnesses that Henry is now the Horseman of War, however gentler he seems?
Will young Molly grow into the Witness Abbie was?

characters.name: Ichabod Crane
characters.line: American citizen and Agency 355 operative; his soul is now owed to Lucifer as the price of Dreyfuss's defeat.

characters.name: Diana Thomas
characters.line: DHS-turned-Agency-355 agent, Ichabod's new partner and Molly's mother — the woman he refused to let become War.

characters.name: Molly Thomas
characters.line: Diana's young daughter, the reincarnation of Abbie's soul and the second Witness at Ichabod's side.

characters.name: Jenny Mills
characters.line: Team member relocated to Washington; the sole Mills sister still holding the front line beside Ichabod.

characters.name: Malcolm Dreyfuss
characters.line: Dead. Immortal tech mogul dragged to Hell by Jobe once the new Stone rendered him mortal again.

characters.name: Henry Parrish
characters.line: Resurrected in a gentler form; now bears the mantle of the Horseman of War in Ichabod's stead.

characters.name: Jobe
characters.line: Dreyfuss's demonic servant; brokered both Dreyfuss's original contract and Ichabod's new deal with Lucifer.

characters.name: Lara
characters.line: Adult Molly from an erased future timeline; chose to travel the world rather than meet her younger self.
